cars.specification_market: Base 851 cc HBR5 Coach in the original manufacturer GT-11 regularisation form drawn up March 23, 1960, referring to recognition on February 19, 1959. The portal metadata instead reports February 20; these identify documents rather than this photographed car’s model year. Exact model-year fields remain unspecified. Base engine/layout/body and four-speed only: no later 954/848 cc option, enlarged bore, individual alternative gear/final-drive set, race brake option, competition weight or ambiguous power figure is imported. The Lane 1955 collection car’s 900 cc / 65 hp and the modified BoneEvil land-speed car are separate references, not this road specification.
cars.summary: The HBR5 carried Deutsch-Bonnet’s small-engine racing know-how into a series-built grand tourer. Its streamlined glass-fibre/polyester body over a lightweight steel backbone, combined with an air-cooled opposed twin and front-wheel drive, makes it a distinctive early lightweight GT. One original HBR5 coach family is counted. DB marque racing achievements explain the engineering context, not the tune or competition history of a particular road car; later engine options, Super Rallye names, body variations and years do not add separate entries.
